question.preamble: The nurse reviews the client’s initial assessment.
question.explanation:
Impaired gas exchange, shown by tachypnea, accessory muscle use, coarse crackles, and green-tinged sputum, is the priority.
The client is afebrile at 99.0°F (37.2°C). Digital clubbing reflects chronic hypoxemia, and the smoking history and medication noncompliance are less acute, nonurgent findings that do not require priority nursing intervention.

question.stem: For each client finding, click to indicate if the finding is consistent with asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), pneumonia, or pulmonary embolism. Each finding may support more than one condition.
question.footnote: Taken from the Maryland Next Gen NCLEX Test Bank Project, University of Maryland School of Nursing: “Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD I)” medical-surgical faculty case study (Suzana Jarquin, MSN, RN, CNEcl, Frederick Community College, September 1, 2022). Available at https://www.nursing.umaryland.edu/mnwc/initiatives/nextgen-nclex/nextgen-nclex-library/ (Faculty Case Studies).
question.explanation:
Clinical manifestations of COPD include dyspnea, cough, an increased anteroposterior diameter (barrel chest), digital clubbing, and expiratory wheezing. A barrel chest and digital clubbing are not manifestations of pneumonia, asthma, or pulmonary embolism.
Dyspnea occurs with all four conditions. Wheezing is rare with pulmonary embolism, and the cough is dry or blood-tinged.

leftContent.intro: A 74-year-old female client is admitted to the emergency department with increasing dyspnea, productive cough, and fatigue.

question.stem: Which orders should the nurse include in the plan of care at this time? Select all that apply.

options.text: Nursing: Administer oxygen via a high-flow oxygen face mask
Nursing: Place client in a high-Fowler’s position
Nursing: Encourage client use of incentive spirometer

question.footnote: Taken from the Maryland Next Gen NCLEX Test Bank Project, University of Maryland School of Nursing: “Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD I)” medical-surgical faculty case study (Suzana Jarquin, MSN, RN, CNEcl, Frederick Community College, September 1, 2022). Available at https://www.nursing.umaryland.edu/mnwc/initiatives/nextgen-nclex/nextgen-nclex-library/ (Faculty Case Studies).
question.preamble: The nurse anticipates the provider’s orders and considers possible nursing interventions.
question.explanation:
The client is experiencing a COPD exacerbation. A high-Fowler’s position and the incentive spirometer maximize lung expansion and improve ventilatory effort. Ipratropium bromide with albuterol and methylprednisolone relieve the airway narrowing and inflammation causing the exacerbation.
Uncontrolled high-flow oxygen in a client with COPD can cause carbon dioxide retention (CO2 narcosis); oxygen is titrated to a target saturation instead. Ondansetron is not indicated because the client has no nausea or vomiting.

question.preamble: The nurse has reviewed the Nurses’ Notes and Vital Signs from 1015 and the Medication Orders. The ipratropium bromide and albuterol treatment is given.
question.explanation:
IV methylprednisolone is ordered now and will reduce airway inflammation to ease breathing. The antibiotic can be given after the corticosteroid.
Albuterol was just given with the ipratropium nebulizer; the client needs to be reassessed to determine whether another PRN dose is needed. The client reports 0/10 pain, so acetaminophen is not needed at this time.

question.preamble: The nurse has reviewed the Nurses’ Notes and Vital Signs from 1045. The nurse administers the ordered medications and reassesses the client at 1045.
question.explanation:
The client’s respiratory rate, breath sounds (crackles now in the upper and lower fields), heart rate, oxygen saturation, and blood pressure have all declined despite the ordered medications. The client no longer has expiratory wheezing, and the temperature is unchanged.
The nurse should promptly alert the provider, as the client’s respiratory status is rapidly deteriorating.
